LESSON: LISTENING FOR INFORMATION

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ARABIC
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.7: Listening for Information

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Listening for Information. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why should we listen attentively?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify members of the extended family from an oral text for information
2. appreciate the roles of extended family members

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: LISTENING FOR INFORMATION
This lesson teaches Listening for Information for Grade 9 ARABIC.

STUDY STEPS
1. identify members of the extended family from an oral text for information
   Practise this until you can do it without help.
2. appreciate the roles of extended family members
   Practise this until you can do it without help.

HOW TO SHOW UNDERSTANDING
Explain the idea in your own words, give one Kenyan example, then complete the practice tasks.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Describe Listening for Information using something at your school.

Example 2: Give a home/community example from your county.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Underline the key ideas about Listening for Information above.
2. Explain Listening for Information to a parent using one local example.
3. Write or draw three things that prove you understand Listening for Information.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Listening for Information with school or home examples.
2. Answer: Why is Listening for Information important for a Grade 9 learner?
3. Prepare a one-minute oral presentation for a parent or teacher.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should we listen attentively?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify members of the extended family from an oral text for information
2. appreciate the roles of extended family members

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
